question: How does this nondual teaching differ from dualistic scriptures regarding the elements?
premises: In dualistic scriptures the elements are treated as separated from the supreme Lord.
This teaching is free from duality.
What is divided in dualism is not divided in the same way here.
inference: Therefore in this nondual system the elements are not regarded as separate from the supreme Lord.
uncertainties: bhūtādīnāṃ may include more than the gross elements, but the verse leaves the scope open.
plain_english: It is said that in dualistic scriptures the elements and so on are treated as separated from the supreme Lord, but in this teaching, which is free from duality, they are not regarded in that way.
